figures.caption: Figure 6: Visual examples of all attacks from Section 4 applied to a single DiffusionDB image watermarked with Pixel Seal. Notation A + B denotes an image first watermarked with method A (victim watermark) and subsequently watermarked with method B (attack watermark).
Table 5: Watermarking methods overview. References under method names point to similar watermarking schemes represented by each method.

Figure 4: Per-image normalized quality degradation introduced by each watermarking method, aggregated over MS-COCO and DiffusionDB. Each box shows the interquartile range, with the solid line indicating the median and the dashed line the mean. Methods with heavier right tails and wider spreads embed a stronger signal on a subset of images, making them harder to overwrite as victims but potentially more disruptive as attack watermarks.

Table 4: Decoder metrics on MS-COCO for our attack vs. baselines. BAclean, BAunwm, BAatk denote the bit accuracy on clean watermarked images, unwatermarked images and attacked watermarked images, respectively. TPR is reported at 1%FPR and #mis denotes the number of images misclassified as unwatermarked. Bold indicates the strongest attack metric achieved per victim method. Effective attacks yield lower BA and TPR, except for Tree-Ring (*ℓ1 distance) and ZoDiac (**p-value) where higher is better. Baseline strengths are chosen to not exceed our attack’s quality degradation, though Rinse 4×Diff still exceeds it even at the lowest strength. See Table 7 in the Appendix for DiffusionDB.
